title.en: Ki Hajar Dewantara: schools for everyone
title.id: Ki Hajar Dewantara: sekolah untuk semua

en: Every year on 2 May, Indonesian schools celebrate National Education Day. The date was chosen because it is the birthday of Ki Hajar Dewantara, one of the most important figures in the history of Indonesian education.

He was born in Yogyakarta in 1889 with the name Raden Mas Soewardi Soerjaningrat. At that time Indonesia was a Dutch colony, and few Indonesian children could go to school, and children from ordinary families had almost no chance.

As a young man, Soewardi became a journalist. He wrote articles criticising the colonial government. One famous article, written in Dutch in 1913, was called 'If I Were a Dutchman'. It said that if he were Dutch, he would be ashamed to celebrate his own country's freedom in a land whose people had lost theirs, and even to ask those people to help pay for the celebration. Because of his writing he was exiled to the Netherlands.
While he was away, he studied education. He came to believe that a good school does not only fill children with facts but helps them grow into free, thoughtful people who love their own culture.

Back home, in 1922, he founded a school in Yogyakarta called Taman Siswa, which means 'garden of students'. Its schools welcomed ordinary Indonesian children and taught in a way that respected Indonesian culture. Later he changed his name to Ki Hajar Dewantara, a simpler name that brought him closer to the people.

After Indonesia became independent, he served as the country's first Minister of Education. One of his teachings, 'Tut Wuri Handayani', means that a teacher supports and encourages from behind. These words still appear on the logo of Indonesia's education ministry today.
id: Setiap tanggal 2 Mei, sekolah-sekolah di Indonesia memperingati Hari Pendidikan Nasional. Tanggal itu dipilih karena merupakan hari lahir Ki Hajar Dewantara, salah satu tokoh terpenting dalam sejarah pendidikan Indonesia.

Ia lahir di Yogyakarta pada tahun 1889 dengan nama Raden Mas Soewardi Soerjaningrat. Saat itu Indonesia masih dijajah Belanda, dan hanya sedikit anak Indonesia yang bisa bersekolah, apalagi anak dari keluarga biasa.

Ketika muda, Soewardi menjadi wartawan. Ia menulis artikel yang mengkritik pemerintah kolonial. Salah satu artikelnya yang terkenal, ditulis dalam bahasa Belanda pada tahun 1913, berjudul 'Seandainya Aku Seorang Belanda'. Isinya: jika ia orang Belanda, ia akan malu merayakan kemerdekaan negerinya di tanah yang rakyatnya dijajah, apalagi meminta rakyat itu ikut membiayai perayaannya. Karena tulisannya itu, ia diasingkan ke Belanda.

Selama di pengasingan, ia mempelajari ilmu pendidikan. Ia yakin bahwa sekolah yang baik tidak hanya mengisi anak dengan fakta, tetapi membantu mereka tumbuh menjadi manusia yang merdeka dan mampu berpikir sendiri serta mencintai budayanya.

Setelah pulang, pada tahun 1922 ia mendirikan sekolah di Yogyakarta bernama Taman Siswa, yang berarti 'taman para murid'. Sekolah-sekolahnya menerima anak-anak Indonesia dari keluarga biasa dan mengajar dengan cara yang menghargai budaya Indonesia. Kemudian ia mengganti namanya menjadi Ki Hajar Dewantara, nama yang lebih sederhana dan mendekatkannya kepada rakyat.

Setelah Indonesia merdeka, ia menjadi Menteri Pendidikan yang pertama. Salah satu ajarannya, 'Tut Wuri Handayani', berarti guru memberi dukungan dan dorongan dari belakang. Kata-kata ini masih ada di logo kementerian pendidikan Indonesia hingga sekarang.

offlineActivity.en: Interview an older family member about their school days. Write three facts and one opinion they share, and compare their school with Taman Siswa's ideas.
offlineActivity.id: Wawancarai anggota keluarga yang lebih tua tentang masa sekolahnya. Tulis tiga fakta dan satu pendapat mereka, lalu bandingkan sekolah mereka dengan gagasan Taman Siswa.

factChecks.claim: Ki Hajar Dewantara was born on 2 May 1889 in Yogyakarta as Raden Mas Soewardi Soerjaningrat.
National Education Day in Indonesia (Hari Pendidikan Nasional) is on 2 May, his birthday.
He wrote a critical Dutch-language article (Als ik een Nederlander was) and was exiled to the Netherlands.
Als ik een Nederlander was was published in 1913.
He founded Taman Siswa in Yogyakarta in 1922.
He was Indonesia's first Minister of Education.
The phrase 'Tut Wuri Handayani' appears on the logo of Indonesia's education ministry.
He studied education during his exile.
